item.subject: Advanced Mathematics
item.stem:
Determine all complex numbers z that satisfy the equation

z + 2 z̄ = 3 + i

where z̄ denotes the conjugate of z .

descriptors:
z = 1 - i. Method: Let z = a + bi.
The given equation is then equivalent to 3a - ib = 3 + i OR 3(a-1) - i (b + 1) = 0.
This equation correctly solved, finding a = 1, b = -1.
z = 1 - i, obtained by any other correct method.
Equation for a,b is derived correctly, but either left unsolved or solution contains numerical or single algebraic error.
Due to numerical error an incorrect equation for a,b has been derived and solved, either correctly or incorrectly.
Other partially correct solutions with correct method but contains a numerical or single algebraic error.

Attempts using b - ai as the conjugate of z, which leads to
z = -3 - i.

Attempts using -z as the conjugate of z which leads to
z = -1/3 + 5/3i.
Attempts using 1/z as the conjugate of z.
Crossed-out, illegible, or impossible to interpret

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it.

step1.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 2-point item with the generalized partial credit model (GPCM), which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 2 or 3 points, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's step 1 parameter d1? In the GPCM, b - d1 is the ability at which earning the first point becomes more likely than earning no point, so a higher d1 means that this point is earned at a lower ability; the steps sum to 0. Choose the value closest to it.
